notes:
Summary: Avalon is a claims automation platform evaluating Redwood Private for claims-triage and document extraction. Strong interest in vpc/on-prem option and full IAM automation (SCIM) for provisioning 1,200+ agents. POC showed promising latency (avg token times within expectations) but stalled on identity integration.

Key requirements: SSO/SAML as first-class auth, SCIM for automated user provisioning, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, KMS integration for encrypted at-rest keys, SOC2 attestation. Must have SCIM before pilot rollout (target pilot launch: 2025-03).

What happened: During security review (01/10) InfoSec said SCIM is a hard requirement for operator onboarding. Current Redwood roadmap items shared verbally do not include guaranteed SCIM delivery before Avalon's pilot window. Avalon paused procurement and started parallel discussions with NimbusSecure who offered SCIM in their enterprise package tied to an accelerated timeline.

Direct quotes: "We can't run a pilot without SCIM — provisioning 1,200 adjusters manually is a non-starter." — Head of IT (Avalon).

POC notes: documents ingestion and reranking performed well; embedding quality sufficient for triage rules. Observability and cost breakdown in Console were liked. Engineering asked about token-level billing export and KV cache persistence (answered). Primary risk remains identity provisioning.

Sales actions taken: AE provided temporary workaround options (manual provisioning + group sync via CSV) and escalated to Product for SCIM prioritization (ticket RDW-4982). Legal requested a DPA and SOC2 evidence; shared security FAQ and SOC2 report link. SE ran a short pilot for two teams (10 users) in VPC environment — positive feedback but flagged provisioning friction.

Current status & next steps: Account effectively stalled in procurement. AE to get commitment from Product on SCIM delivery date by 2025-02-05; if no firm date, Avalon will proceed with NimbusSecure. Legal to finish DPA if product commitment provided. CSM Diego tentatively assigned once procurement completes.

Linked artifacts: Fireflies IDs (ff_2024-12-03_avalon-demo, ff_2025-01-10_security-review), Drive POC deck, security FAQ. Jira/Support: INF-11234 (request for SCIM feature), RDW-4982 (private deployment questions).

Notes on competitive dynamics: NimbusSecure pitched identity-first enterprise package and offered to sign a timeline in the contract. Avalon is price-sensitive but prioritizes security compliance/features over a small delta in cost.

Why closed-lost is possible: Without SCIM commitment and a named delivery window, Avalon cannot justify disrupting their rollout and is contractually aligned with their internal compliance calendar (pilot launch fixed). Sales recommendation: either secure a product-level commitment and a phased SCIM beta for Avalon or accept this as closed-lost and log lessons learned (esp. identity automation as a gating feature for larger mid-market insurance customers).
